data.name: Shivashankar
data.long_meaning: Shivashankar is a name derived from the Sanskrit words ‘Shiva’ and ‘Shankar’. Shiva is the name of the Hindu god of destruction, time, and creation. data.cultural_impact: The name Shivashankar is rooted in ancient Hindu mythology and carries significant cultural importance. Shiva is known as the destroyer of evil and the purifier of the universe. He is a significant deity in Hinduism, and his worship is widespread across India and beyond. The name Shivashankar acknowledges and pays homage to his divine power. Likewise, Shankar as the god of mountains represents the strength and stability of nature. Mountains are considered sacred in Hinduism and are often associated with spiritual growth and self-realization. The fusion of these two powerful concepts in a name serves to remind us of the vast and intricate tapestry of Hindu traditions and myths.
data.spiritual_significance: On a deeper level, Shivashankar as a name signifies the union of the divine and the material world. Shiva's destructive power represents a necessary force for purification and renewal in the universe. The mountain, symbolizing stability and strength, also has spiritual significance as it is oftentimes seen as a place for spiritual retreat and communion with higher powers. The combination of Shiva and Shankar in this name serves as a constant reminder of the power of the divine to transform and bring a sense of balance and stability to life. It is a testament to the profound spiritual beliefs that have influenced the Hindu culture for centuries.

historical_references.reference: Shivashankar was a title given to Shiva during the Chalukya dynasty of Karnataka, India. It is believed that King Vijayaditya (1086-1100 CE) built the Shivashankar Temple in honor of this deity.

historical_references.reference: Shankaracharya Shivabhutendra was a Hindu philosopher, theologian, and saint, who lived during the 17th century in southern India. He wrote extensively on Shiva philosophy and is considered a major figure in the history of Shivism. Shivashankar is a combination of his personal name Shivabhutendra and the title Shankar, which refers to Lord Shiva.
